admission.justification: The documented rejected import-cycle and extraction alternatives constrain where the retained control can live and how fixed-page rows obtain it.

alternatives.option: Keep rowDirectGrant and DirectGrantControl byte-identical in taskReader; pass a LeafExtra function to the three leaf row kinds and draw selected-leaf control below DocHead.
alternatives.reason: Preserves landed control and test IDs while avoiding a reader/groups import cycle and keeps the bounded L127 head unchanged.

alternatives.option: Import the reader control directly into task-groups.
alternatives.reason: The reader already imports groups; reversing the dependency introduces a lint-rejected import cycle.
alternatives.reconsider_when: An admitted dependency restructuring provides an acyclic owner without changing the preserved control contract.

alternatives.option: Extract the landed control into a new source file during this sync.
alternatives.reason: Moves the incoming control out of its landed owner and gives an added file the three inherited diagnostics; not admitted by the current port/closeout scope.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The inherited lint debt is repaired under its owner and a separately admitted extraction preserves the control and dependencies.

consequences: Selected-leaf badge is below the head; row badge is beside its link. These are explicit placement differences, not layout equivalence.
Only authored leaf rows/selected leaves receive the control; sprint/master exclusions and unchanged control/test bytes remain as source-qualified.
No new execution campaign, no whole-feature or MEMORY acceptance is implied by this decision.
context: The direct-execution grant of MIK-R94 is shown in the task pages of MIK-R127 as it was on the pages before: on a master page each leaf row carries, beside its link, the badge with the giver where the leaf has a grant and the developer's control where the leaf is an authored task; on a task page the badge and the control stand under the head. The control and its helper are the landed code of MIK-R94, unchanged; only their call sites are placed in the new page structure. The rows take what the page adds to a leaf row as a function, because the row file cannot import the reader without an import cycle. Producer evidence: notes/reports/worker/7b2c4e19-5d63-4a8f-b1e0-127000000a01/evidence-f9-on-857c7e5f/checks/l94-dashboard-tests.log (the nine tests of dashboard/src/panels/detail-panel/directGrantControl.test.tsx and the three of the grant's data module pass; the test file holds the bytes of the head); notes/reports/worker/7b2c4e19-5d63-4a8f-b1e0-127000000a01/sync-port-F9-on-857c7e5f.md (the ported hunks by file and line, the landed blocks compared byte for byte); notes/reports/worker/7b2c4e19-5d63-4a8f-b1e0-127000000a01/lint-record-F9-on-857c7e5f.md (the lint shows the three findings of the landed control and no other) Independent source-only placement/sync PASS: code-F9-857c7e5f-source-delta-verdict.md; no independent whole MEMORY grade or new execution.
